title: Wheel metadata omits runtime dependencies required by the app
reasoning: The installable project metadata only includes a subset of the runtime dependencies listed in requirements.txt. A user or deployment installing from the wheel or with `pip install .` will not get Alembic, bcrypt, python-jose, youtube-transcript-api, or pytz, even though the README describes migrations, authentication, newsletter/content processing, and scheduling behavior that depend on those dependency groups. This creates release artifacts that can import or start successfully in one path but fail at runtime in another.
reproduction: Build/install from pyproject metadata only, for example `pip install .`, then exercise startup migrations/auth code paths that import omitted packages such as `alembic`, `bcrypt`, or `jose`.
recommendation: Make `pyproject.toml` the authoritative runtime dependency list by adding the missing runtime packages, or explicitly stop publishing/installing from pyproject metadata and document requirements.txt as the only supported install path. Prefer keeping requirements.txt generated or synchronized from pyproject to avoid drift.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided, and there is no package-install smoke test proving that a wheel or `pip install .` environment can start the service.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a packaging smoke test that creates a clean environment, installs the project from `pyproject.toml`, and imports/starts the FastAPI app plus migration/auth modules.
minimumFixScope: Update `pyproject.toml` `project.dependencies` to include all runtime dependencies currently required by the application and keep `requirements.txt` aligned.
